subject: general
question:
Consider the following statements about service rules in table tennis:

1) At 10-10, service alternates every two points.

2) In the final doubles game, receiver order changes when one side reaches 5 points.

Which of the above is/are **correct**?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In table tennis, service alternates every point once the score reaches 10-10 (deuce), rather than every two points as stated in the question. Hence, Statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• In doubles matches, the receiver order changes after one side reaches 5 points in the final game (often referred to as the deciding game). This rule ensures fairness by balancing the playing sides. Statement 2 is correct.
 
• The rules for service and receiver order in table tennis are specified by the International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF) and are strictly adhered to in official matches.
 
• Table tennis service rules are designed to ensure fairness, prevent predictability, and maintain the competitive nature of the game.
 
• Statement 2 aligns with the official rules of ITTF regarding receiver order in the final doubles game.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **General Table Tennis Rules:**

 
 
• Table tennis matches consist of either best-of-five or best-of-seven games, depending on the tournament format.
 
• The service rules require the ball to be tossed at least 16 cm vertically and hit behind the end line of the table.
 
• A game is won by the player or team that first scores 11 points with at least a 2-point lead.
 
• The ITTF governs the rules and regulations for table tennis worldwide.
